description: Long monthly planning meeting (about 20 minutes, four topics, tasks spread through it, one explicitly unassigned task). Invented people and facts.
lines: Okay, let's start. This is the monthly planning meeting. We have the roadmap, hiring, the offsite, and the support backlog.
Let's start with the roadmap because that's the big one.
So on the roadmap, the main question is whether offline sync goes into the June release or slips to July.
From the engineering side, sync is about seventy percent done. Conflict resolution is the hard part left.
Realistically three weeks, and then a week of testing on bad networks.
That puts us right at the end of June with no slack at all.
Customers keep asking for it though. It came up in four of the last five sales calls.
I'd rather ship it in July and have it work than ship a broken version in June.
Same. A sync bug that loses data would be much worse than a delay.
Okay. Decision: offline sync moves to the July release. June ships the reporting improvements only.
Then I need to tell the customers who were promised June.
Yes. Lena, can you let those customers know about the new date?
I'll email them this week and offer a call if anyone wants one.
For the June release, the reporting work is basically finished. Just the export to spreadsheet is left.
That's a two day job. Kofi started it last week.
Good. Let's move on to hiring.
We have budget for two engineers this quarter. We've interviewed six people so far.
Two of them were strong. The backend candidate from last Tuesday was the best I've seen this year.
I agree on her. The other strong one was the mobile developer, but he wants to be fully remote.
Fully remote is fine for mobile. We already have two remote engineers.
What about the salary range? The backend candidate asked for more than the band.
We can stretch the band a little for someone that good. I'll talk to finance about it.
If we wait too long she'll take another offer. She said she has one on the table.
Then let's move quickly. I'll get an answer from finance by Friday.
Let's do a final round with him next week. Marcus, can you set up the final interview?
Sure, I'll schedule it for Tuesday or Wednesday.
So for the offsite, I looked at three places. The lake house, the city hotel, and the farm.
The lake house is the cheapest but it's two and a half hours away.
Two and a half hours each way eats most of a day.
The city hotel is close but it's expensive, about twice the lake house.
The farm is an hour away, has meeting rooms, and it's in the middle on price.
The farm sounds like the right balance. Does anyone object?
No, the farm is fine with me.
Fine with me too, as long as the Wi-Fi works. We tried to demo there once and it was bad.
I'll ask them about the Wi-Fi before we book.
Okay, the farm, pending Wi-Fi. What dates?
They have the second week of September free.
Second week of September works. Lena, go ahead and book it if the Wi-Fi checks out.
The backlog is at one hundred and forty tickets. It was ninety a month ago.
A lot of those are the same password reset problem on older Android phones.
If we fixed that one bug, we'd close maybe forty tickets at once.
I know what the cause is. It's the old browser on those phones not supporting the new login form.
A day, maybe two, to add a fallback form.
That's clearly worth it. Marcus, please take the password reset fix.
Okay, I'll do the fallback login form next.
The rest of the backlog is mixed. Billing questions, feature requests, a few real bugs.
Maybe we should write a help page for the billing questions. They're mostly the same three questions.
Good idea. Somebody should write that help page, but let's not assign it today, the team is full.
One more thing on support. The weekend coverage rota ends this month.
Let's continue the same rota for another quarter. No changes.
Okay, I think that's everything. To recap the decisions: sync moves to July, the farm for the offsite, and we move fast on the backend hire.
Thanks everyone, see you next month.
